issues.issue: The Bank may change any term "at any time" and give only "such notice of the change as we determine is appropriate," a self-judging notice standard with no fixed content or timing.
It cannot be squared with Part II's Fees & Charges clause, which promises notice "at least thirty (30) days in advance of any changes to these fees."
"Accounts" is redefined for Part II to include ALL personal deposit Accounts, which is broader than the Definitions section's "Account" and creates two operative meanings of the same term.
It conditions the disclosed APY on maintaining the minimum tier balance "each day," while the tier clauses (2A-2E) say the rate for the appropriate tier is paid on the full balance in the Account.

It fixes a rate for "Non-personal TD Relationship Savings accounts," although Part II states that the Accounts covered are ALL personal deposit Accounts and the instrument is a Personal Deposit Account Agreement.
A one-off "Immediate transfer" is made to qualify, although the immediately preceding definition requires a qualifying transfer to be a "recurring transfer."
The clause directs the reader to "The Chart on page 31" while the balance tier structure it describes is set out immediately below it on the same page, a cross-reference error.
The penalty table uses the shorthand "90 days < 1 year" and "1 year < 2 years," leaving the endpoints of each band, and the treatment of a term of exactly one or two years, unstated.
The table expressly applies its penalties to "No Catch" CDs, while the "No Catch" CD clause promises one principal withdrawal during the term with no penalty.
"More than one withdrawal of principal during the term of this CD may result in a penalty" does not say when or what penalty, leaving the customer's exposure indeterminate.

The promise of a penalty-free principal withdrawal conflicts with the Early Withdrawal Penalties table, which lists "No Catch" CDs among the terms carrying interest penalties, and with its rule that no principal may be withdrawn without the Bank's consent.
A single "Immediate transfer" is made to qualify although the definition in the preceding sub-paragraph requires a recurring transfer of at least $25.
The promise of thirty days' advance notice of fee changes conflicts with the Amendments clause, which reserves the right to give only such notice as the Bank determines is appropriate.
This $100-deposit Direct Deposit bonus and the $100-deposit cash bonus in the first paragraph are triggered by the same act, yet each says it "cannot be combined with any other offer."

Eligibility turns on depositing "money not already on deposit at TD Bank" / "new to bank money," a source-tracing test the clause does not explain, and "Maximum deposit limits may apply" states no limit.

The Policy is applied to "all transaction accounts such as Checking and Interest Bearing Checking Accounts, and to Money Market, Savings, and Time Accounts," with "Time Accounts" nowhere defined and "such as" leaving the class open.
The "general policy" of first-Business-Day availability is stated flatly, yet the Longer Delays and Special Rules For New Accounts clauses permit second-, fifth- and seventh-day availability.
"[T]he earliest time that we stop accepting deposits ... for same-day credit is 8pm" states only a floor, not the actual cut-off, and the sentence runs on into "Thus" with no punctuation.
Night depository funds are deemed deposited on the next Business Day the Bank is open, while Part VI's Processing Deposits clause allows two Business Days after receipt of the bag before credit.

Same-day availability of $100 from non-cash teller deposits is hard to reconcile with the Longer Delays clause, which makes "[t]he first $200 of your deposit" available no later than the first Business Day after deposit.

The list of grounds for extended delay includes the open-ended "we believe a check you deposited will not be paid" and "there is an emergency, such as failure of communications or computer equipment," the latter an illustration rather than a defined class.
